mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series 325e engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 325e engine replacement typically costs £1,800-£3,500 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, or £2,500-£4,800 fitted by a specialist. Used engines start from around £800-£1,500, while reconditioned units range from £1,500 to £2,200.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing belt failure in a BMW 325e?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most critical sign is simply age - if the belt is over 4 years old or has covered more than 50,000 miles, it needs replacing regardless of symptoms. Other warning signs include a squealing noise from the front of the engine, visible cracks or fraying on the belt, or rough running.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 3 Series 325e?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's condition and your intentions. A 325e in average condition is worth approximately £3,217-£11,824. For a car valued under £5,000, a used engine or repair is often more sensible. For a clean, low-mileage example with rising classic values, a rebuilt engine with warranty is a justifiable investment.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 325e and 325i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 325e uses the M20B27 'Eta' engine - a 2.7-litre long-stroke design producing 121hp and 170 lb-ft of torque at just 3,250rpm. The 325i uses the M20B25 - a 2.5-litre short-stroke design producing 168hp but with less low-end torque. The 'e' stands for 'Eta' - efficiency.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series 325e engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 3 Series 325e engine replacement takes 2-3 days for a specialist workshop, assuming the replacement engine is available. The E30 platform is relatively straightforward to work on.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a BMW 325e replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt and reconditioned BMW 3 Series 325e engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with a shorter warranty (30-90 days) depending on the supplier - always confirm exact terms before purchasing.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series 325e - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 325e (the 'e' standing for 'Eta' - the Greek letter used by BMW to denote efficiency) was introduced in 1984 as a torque-focused, fuel-efficient alternative to the higher-revving 325i. Powered by the 2.7-litre M20B27 six-cylinder, the 325e prioritised low-end grunt over peak power, making it a relaxed and economical cruiser. The 325e was produced throughout the E30 generation's lifespan, with a catalyst-equipped version arriving in 1985.

milestones.description: 1985 (E30 pre-facelift) - M20B27, 2.7-litre 12-valve SOHC, 121hp, Bosch Motronic fuel injection
1987 (E30 facelift, catalyst) - M20B27, 2.7-litre 12-valve SOHC, 122hp (catalyst version 129hp in some markets), 230Nm torque
1988 (E30 facelift, late) - M20B27, 2.7-litre 12-valve SOHC, continued with minor emissions updates

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series 325e Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 325e is powered by the M20B27 'Eta' six-cylinder - a long-stroke, torque-focused engine that is generally robust when properly maintained. However, age and neglect bring several well-documented failure points. The M20B27 is an interference engine, meaning timing belt failure is catastrophic. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include new timing components and are backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Belt Failure - Why the BMW 3 Series 325e M20B27 is an Interference Engine
problems.rootCause: The M20B27 uses a rubber timing belt, not a chain. Over time, the belt stretches, frays, or snaps. As an interference engine, if the timing belt breaks, the camshaft stops turning while the crankshaft continues - valves collide with pistons, bending valves and often destroying the cylinder head.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New belt, tensioner, water pump, seals - the 'full kit'
repairOptions.longevity: Best done every 50k miles or 4 years - cheap insurance against catastrophic failure

repairOptions.tier: Cylinder head rebuild (after belt failure, minor damage)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove head, replace bent valves, skim head, new gasket set
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if pistons are undamaged and head is not cracked

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if belt snapped at speed causing extensive damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series 325e is worth approximately £3,217-£11,824 depending on condition. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: a used engine or timing belt replacement typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car as a long-term classic. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£12,000+: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability - especially for a matching-numbers car.
problems.recommendation: Prevention is everything on the M20B27. If you have no record of the timing belt being changed in the last 4 years or 50,000 miles, replace it immediately - a £400-£700 preventative job is far cheaper than a £1,800-£3,500 engine replacement. If the belt has already snapped, assess the damage carefully; if the head is cracked or pistons damaged, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is the most reliable path forward.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M20B27 BMW 3 Series 325e engine prices

problems.h4: Vacuum Leaks & Idle Issues - The M20B27's Sensitivity to Ageing Rubber
problems.typicalFailureMileage: Age-related - rubber components degrade regardless of mileage
problems.rootCause: The M20B27 is very sensitive to vacuum leaks. Over time, rubber intake boots, vacuum hoses, and intake manifold gaskets become brittle and crack, allowing unmetered air into the engine. This causes rough idle, stalling, and poor drivability.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Smoke test, replace cracked hoses and gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: First step for any idle or drivability issue

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with all new gaskets and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Only if the engine has been severely neglected or suffered other major failure

problems.recommendation: Vacuum leaks are one of the most common and easily fixable issues on the M20B27. A specialist smoke test will quickly identify the source. Replacing all the perished rubber hoses is a relatively inexpensive job that transforms drivability.
